label: Personality
value: Anne is intensely imaginative.
unit: Anne is intensely imaginative, romantic, and passionate, experiencing life's joys and sorrows with extreme vividness. She possesses a lively wit, a deep appreciation for nature and beauty, and an eager desire to win the affection of those around her. Though prone to impulsive mistakes and occasional dramatic outbursts of temper, she is fiercely loyal, generous, and quick to repent. As she matures, she develops greater self-control, quiet reflection, and a strong sense of duty without losing her innate capacity for joy and wonder.

label: Goals
value: To be a good teacher and save Marilla's eyesight

label: History
value: Anne Shirley arrives in Avonlea
unit: Anne Shirley arrives in Avonlea on Prince Edward Island after being mistakenly brought from an orphan asylum by Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert, who had intended to adopt a boy. Despite initial intentions to send her back, Marilla and Matthew decide to keep her at Green Gables. Anne quickly makes a bosom friend in Diana Barry and enters Avonlea school, where an incident involving Gilbert Blythe calling her 'Carrots' starts a long-standing academic rivalry and grudge. Over the next few years, Anne gets into various humorous mishaps, such as inadvertently getting Diana intoxicated on currant wine, accidentally dyeing her hair green, and falling off a roof on a dare. Her resourcefulness shines when she saves Diana's little sister Minnie May from croup. She joins the Queen's Academy class, earns her teacher's license in one year, and wins the prestigious Avery Scholarship. However, after Matthew suddenly dies of a heart attack and Marilla faces failing eyesight, Anne selflessly gives up her college scholarship to stay at Green Gables, taking the Avonlea schoolteaching position instead. She helps found the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, helps raise the Keith twins, and finally reconciles her long-standing feud with Gilbert Blythe, becoming close friends as they both prepare for their futures.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye was taken in by Mr. George Pye.
unit: Anthony Pye was taken in by his aunt and uncle, Mr. and Mrs. George Pye, and enrolled at Avonlea school under Anne Shirley. Holding the view that female teachers were useless, he maintained a sullen and mocking attitude toward Anne. On a particularly stressful day at school, he placed a live mouse in Anne's desk; when confronted, he insolently admitted his guilt, prompting Anne to lose her temper and whip him with a pointer. Surprising everyone, the punishment won Anthony's respect, as he declared the whipping was as good as a man's. Following this incident, he became helpful and polite to Anne, even defending her against other boys when she eventually announced her resignation.

label: History
value: Billy Andrews is a young man.
unit: Billy Andrews is a young man from Avonlea who lives with his family. When his sister Jane was unable to dry her tears at school, she borrowed a handkerchief from him. He later drives his sister Jane, Anne Shirley, and Diana Barry to the White Sands Hotel in his family's double-seated buggy for a benefit concert. During the drive, he insists that Anne sit beside him on the front seat, though he grins and chuckles without being able to think of answers to her conversation in time. After the concert, he waits for the girls outside with the team, having fled the hotel in fear of being invited to the formal late-night supper.

label: History
value: Leonora Bowman came to live at Echo Lodge.
unit: Leonora Bowman came to live at Echo Lodge as a hired girl for Miss Lavendar Lewis, following in the footsteps of her three older sisters. Miss Lavendar dubbed her 'Charlotta the Fourth' to keep her sisters' identities straight, a name she accepted cheerfully. She performed household chores and accommodated Miss Lavendar's imaginative whims, including playing along with her imaginary tea parties. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally stumbled upon Echo Lodge, Charlotta helped entertain them and immediately formed a deep admiration for Anne. Over time, she confided her worries to Anne about Miss Lavendar's health and loneliness, especially after a visit from Stephen Irving's son, Paul. When Stephen Irving returned to court Miss Lavendar, Charlotta eagerly assisted with the preparations for the wedding. Following Miss Lavendar's marriage to Stephen Irving, plans were made for Charlotta to move to Boston with them in the autumn to continue serving the family.

label: History
value: Davy Keith was orphaned in East Grafton.
unit: Davy Keith and his twin sister Dora were orphaned in East Grafton when their mother passed away. Because their uncle in British Columbia could not immediately care for them, Marilla Cuthbert brought them to live at Green Gables. Davy quickly established a reputation for endless pranks and unruly behavior, such as dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck in church, tricking his sister into a pigpen, and putting a toad in Marilla's bed. After shutting Dora in Mr. Harrison's toolhouse and lying about her whereabouts, Davy was brought to tears by Anne Shirley's grief and promised never to tell a falsehood again. He entered Avonlea School under Anne's tutelage, where he gradually learned better manners and strived to emulate his rival, Paul Irving. Following the death of his uncle Richard, a trust fund was established for Davy and Dora, securing their permanent home at Green Gables.

After shutting Dora in Mr. Harrison's toolhouse and lying about her whereabouts, Davy was brought to tears by Anne Shirley's grief and promised never to tell a falsehood again. He entered Avonlea School under Anne's tutelage, where he gradually learned better manners and strived to emulate his rival, Paul Irving. Following the death of his uncle Richard, a trust fund was established for Davy and Dora, securing their permanent home at Green Gables.

value: Diana is cheerful.
unit: Diana is cheerful, good-tempered, and highly practical, often serving as a sensible counterweight to Anne's vivid, romantic imagination. Although she lacks Anne's intense imaginative flights, she is an affectionate, loyal, and devoted companion. She loves reading and playing games, though she can be timid about anything dangerous or superstitious. She possesses a merry disposition and enjoys simple pleasures, social gatherings, and fun with her peers.

label: History
value: Diana returned home from a visit to Carmody.
unit: Upon returning home from a visit to Carmody, Diana met Anne Shirley and the two girls solemnly swore an oath of eternal friendship in the Barry garden. Shortly after, Diana accidentally became intoxicated at Green Gables when Anne unknowingly served her currant wine instead of raspberry cordial, causing Mrs. Barry to strictly forbid Diana from playing with Anne. However, when her little sister Minnie May fell gravely ill with croup during her parents' absence, Anne saved the child's life, prompting Mrs. Barry to forgive Anne and restore the girls' friendship. Together with Anne, Diana joined the Avonlea school, participated in schoolhouse plays, the Debating Club concert, and the story club, and helped found the Avonlea Village Improvement Society as its treasurer. Although she did not join the Queen's class to pursue a teaching career, she remained Anne's constant confidante and supported her during her examinations and college preparations. During their late teens, Diana became romantically involved with Fred Wright, eventually becoming engaged to him.

label: History
value: Dora's mother died in East Grafton.
unit: Following the death of her mother in East Grafton, Dora and her twin brother Davy were taken in by Marilla Cuthbert and Anne Shirley at Green Gables for the winter, as their uncle Richard Keith could not immediately care for them. Unlike Davy, Dora adjusted smoothly to life at Green Gables, behaving politely and assisting with household errands. During the local Aid Society meeting, Davy tricked her into walking the pigpen fence, resulting in her falling in and getting thoroughly soaked when he attempted to pump her clean. When school opened, she was assigned to sit with Mirabel Cotton, who frightened her with stories of dead relatives and ghosts until Anne intervened. She began cultivating her own small garden plot in the spring, successfully growing vegetables through careful tending. In the autumn, word arrived that her uncle Richard had died, leaving a trust fund for the twins, ensuring that Dora would remain permanently at Green Gables.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea
unit: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea after three years in Alberta with his father and resumed his studies at the Avonlea school. On his first afternoon back, he teased new student Anne Shirley by calling her 'Carrots,' prompting her to smash a slate over his head and declare a lifelong grudge against him. Despite Gilbert's public apologies and attempts to make peace over the years, Anne steadfastly ignored him while they engaged in a fierce academic rivalry. Both were promoted to the fifth class, joined Miss Stacy's Queen's Academy preparation class, and ultimately tied for first place on the Island-wide Entrance examinations to Queen's Academy, where Gilbert won the bronze medal for classics. Due to his father's financial constraints, Gilbert took the White Sands schoolteaching position for a year to earn money for college. Learning that Anne wished to stay in Avonlea to care for Marilla Cuthbert after Matthew's death, Gilbert generously gave up the Avonlea school so she could have it instead. Touched by his sacrifice, Anne thanked him on Barry's hill and offered her forgiveness, beginning a warm friendship and academic partnership. After a year of teaching in White Sands, during which he helped organize the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, Gilbert won the Governor-General's medal at Queen's and prepared to attend Redmond College alongside Anne.

label: History
value: Mr. J. A. Harrison originally lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick.
unit: Mr. J. A. Harrison originally lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick. After his sister passed away, he married Emily Scott, but their marriage suffered due to clash of habits—especially her obsession with extreme tidiness and her dislike of his profane parrot, Ginger. Following a severe quarrel over the parrot during a visit from local ministers, Emily left him, and Mr. Harrison subsequently relocated to Avonlea, buying Robert Bell's farm and living as an eccentric, self-proclaimed bachelor. He first met Anne Shirley when her Jersey cow repeatedly broke into his oatfield, leading to an angry confrontation. Shortly afterward, Anne accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's Jersey cow instead of her own, but when she went to confess and make amends, he forgave her good-naturedly and accepted her cow in exchange, sparking a warm neighborly friendship between them. Mr. Harrison supported Anne's Village Improvement Society projects, though he initially refused to contribute financially.

label: History
value: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea as a classmate and friend of Anne Shirley and Diana Barry. She attended the local school under Mr. Phillips and later Miss Stacy, joining the Queen's class to prepare for a teaching license. During her school years, she participated in local events such as the Sunday School picnic, the Christmas concert, and the youth Story Club, where she was noted for writing sensible, non-romantic stories. She passed her Entrance Examinations successfully and attended Queen's Academy in Charlottetown, where she distinguished herself in the domestic science course and earned her Second Class teacher's license. After graduating, she accepted a position as teacher at the Newbridge school, and later took the school in Carmody when it became vacant.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis lived a secluded life.
unit: Miss Lavendar Lewis lived a secluded life in a secluded stone house called Echo Lodge in Middle Grafton, kept company by a series of young handmaidens whom she called 'Charlotta'. Twenty-five years prior, she had been engaged to Stephen Irving, but a silly quarrel and her own proud sulkiness parted them, leading Stephen to leave for the United States. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry stumbled upon her hidden home while lost and immediately befriended her, enjoying her imaginative hospitality. Later, Anne brought Stephen's son, Paul Irving, to visit Miss Lavendar, which eventually led to Stephen Irving returning to see her. The two reconciled their old misunderstanding, renewed their engagement, and were married in the garden under the honeysuckle trellis before departing for a new life together in Boston.

Anne Shirley and Diana Barry stumbled upon her hidden home while lost and immediately befriended her, enjoying her imaginative hospitality. Later, Anne brought Stephen's son, Paul Irving, to visit Miss Lavendar, which eventually led to Stephen Irving returning to see her. The two reconciled their old misunderstanding, renewed their engagement, and were married in the garden under the honeysuckle trellis before departing for a new life together in Boston.

label: Personality
value: Marilla has a rigid conscience.
unit: Marilla is a woman of narrow experience and rigid conscience, possessing an exacting, orderly nature that values neatness and duty above all else. Though outwardly stern, sarcastic, and unaccustomed to expressing affection, she harbors a deep, quiet tenderness and a dry sense of humor. She is firmly resolute in her decisions once made, yet possesses a practical fairness that allows her to admit her own mistakes. Over the years, her upbringing of Anne softens her rigid outlook and renders her much more mellow and tolerant.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived a quiet life.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived a quiet, solitary life at Green Gables with her shy brother Matthew. Deciding to adopt an orphan boy to assist Matthew on the farm, they were mistakenly sent an eleven-year-old girl named Anne Shirley. Though initially determined to return her, Marilla yielded to Matthew's wishes and agreed to raise the girl. Over the following years, Marilla conscientiously undertook Anne's upbringing, striving to correct her impulsive daydreams while gradually coming to love her as her own flesh and blood. When Matthew died suddenly of a heart attack following a bank failure, Marilla faced the prospect of selling Green Gables due to failing health and threatened blindness. However, Anne sacrificed her college scholarship to remain in Avonlea to teach and care for Marilla. To make the arrangement sustainable, Marilla invited her newly widowed friend, Rachel Lynde, to move into Green Gables, allowing Anne to pursue her college degree at Redmond while Marilla remained supported at home.

Though initially determined to return her, Marilla yielded to Matthew's wishes and agreed to raise the girl. Over the following years, Marilla conscientiously undertook Anne's upbringing, striving to correct her impulsive daydreams while gradually coming to love her as her own flesh and blood. When Matthew died suddenly of a heart attack following a bank failure, Marilla faced the prospect of selling Green Gables due to failing health and threatened blindness. However, Anne sacrificed her college scholarship to remain in Avonlea to teach and care for Marilla. To make the arrangement sustainable, Marilla invited her newly widowed friend, Rachel Lynde, to move into Green Gables, allowing Anne to pursue her college degree at Redmond while Marilla remained supported at home.

value: Matthew was extraordinarily shy.
unit: Matthew was extraordinarily shy and silent, dreading strangers and particularly all women except his sister Marilla and Mrs. Rachel Lynde. Despite his painful shyness, he had a deeply gentle, sympathetic, and indulgent nature. He was a quiet listener who appreciated lively chatter when no response was demanded of him, and he silently clung to his opinions with surprising persistence.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lived a quiet, secluded life.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived a quiet, secluded life farming Green Gables with his sister Marilla. Reaching the age of sixty and suffering from heart trouble, he agreed with Marilla to adopt an orphan boy from Nova Scotia to assist with farm work. When Matthew drove to Bright River station to collect the child, he was met by Anne Shirley instead, whom he lacked the heart to turn away. During the drive home, he was instantly charmed by her imaginative chatter and convinced Marilla to let her stay at Green Gables. Over the next four years, Matthew became Anne's steadfast champion and 'kindred spirit,' frequently indulging her wishes, buying her chocolate sweeties, insisting she be allowed to attend social events, and purchasing a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for her Christmas gift. He took immense pride in her academic achievements, encouraging her dreams and assuring her he was prouder of her than a dozen boys. In her second year of teaching, when Anne passed her entrance examinations to Queen's Academy at the top of the Island, Matthew expressed his deep pride in her. Shortly after her graduation, Matthew received a newspaper reporting the sudden collapse of the Abbey Bank where all his and Marilla's savings were kept; the shock caused an instantaneous, fatal heart attack in the doorway of Green Gables.

When Matthew drove to Bright River station to collect the child, he was met by Anne Shirley instead, whom he lacked the heart to turn away. During the drive home, he was instantly charmed by her imaginative chatter and convinced Marilla to let her stay at Green Gables. Over the next four years, Matthew became Anne's steadfast champion and 'kindred spirit,' frequently indulging her wishes, buying her chocolate sweeties, insisting she be allowed to attend social events, and purchasing a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for her Christmas gift. He took immense pride in her academic achievements, encouraging her dreams and assuring her he was prouder of her than a dozen boys. In her second year of teaching, when Anne passed her entrance examinations to Queen's Academy at the top of the Island, Matthew expressed his deep pride in her. Shortly after her graduation, Matthew received a newspaper reporting the sudden collapse of the Abbey Bank where all his and Marilla's savings were kept; the shock caused an instantaneous, fatal heart attack in the doorway of Green Gables.

value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster of the Avonlea school.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster of the Avonlea school, where he focused much of his attention on preparing older pupils for Queen's Academy. During his tenure, he frequently disciplined Anne Shirley, including making her stand before the blackboard for cracking her slate over Gilbert Blythe's head and forcing her to sit with Gilbert for being late. He also participated in local events, such as giving an address at the Debating Club concert. At the end of June, his term as teacher concluded and he departed from Avonlea, making an emotional farewell speech to his pupils.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived at Lynde's Hollow
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived at Lynde's Hollow where she closely observed all happenings along the Avonlea main road. When Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert decided to adopt a boy, she expressed strong disapproval of the foolish risk, and was astonished when a girl named Anne Shirley arrived instead. Upon meeting Anne, Rachel bluntly criticized her red hair and skinny appearance, provoking a passionate outburst from the child. After Anne offered a dramatic and thorough apology, Rachel forgave her and grew to like her. Throughout Anne's school years, Rachel frequently gave advice on her upbringing and cautioned Marilla against modern innovations. Following the death of her husband, Thomas Lynde, Rachel faced the necessity of selling her mortgaged farm. Rather than leave Avonlea to live with her daughter, she accepted Marilla Cuthbert's invitation to move into Green Gables, allowing Anne to attend Redmond College while Rachel kept Marilla company.

label: History
value: Ruby attended the Avonlea school
unit: Ruby attended the Avonlea school alongside Anne Shirley and her friends, participating in schoolroom gossip and playground games. She joined the Avonlea school concert as a performer in dialogues and tableaux, and later became a member of the girls' Story Club, writing overly sentimental stories. Along with Anne and other classmates, she studied under Miss Stacy for the Queen's Academy entrance examinations and successfully passed. During her year at Queen's in Charlottetown, she pursued a Second Class teacher's license and was noted as the handsomest girl of her year. After graduating, she secured a position as the schoolteacher at Carmody.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy is engaged as the new schoolteacher in Avonlea.
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy is engaged as the new schoolteacher in Avonlea, becoming the first woman to hold the position there. She introduces several novel practices, including physical culture exercises, nature study field afternoons, and bi-weekly recitation sessions. In November of her first year, she organizes a Christmas concert to raise money for a schoolhouse flag. Recognizing the potential of her advanced pupils, she forms an extra class after school hours to prepare them for the Queen's Academy entrance examinations. Although offered a position at a school in her home district for the following year, she decides to remain in Avonlea to see her students through their examinations. Her entire class passes the entrance exams successfully, with her pupils Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe tying for first place on the island.
